literal: When I return to the capital I will first behead this slave.
idiomatic: When I return to the capital I will behead this fellow first.

literal: Bi's head was pointed; Shizu often called him Brush Head, so people called him Pen Lord.
idiomatic: Bi had a pointed head; Shizu nicknamed him Brush Head, and people called him Pen Lord.

literal: Bi's subordinate officials were terrified, fearing execution.
idiomatic: Bi's staff were terrified they would all be executed.

literal: Bi told them: "I think that in serving one's lord, making the hunt ill-suited to roaming sport is a small fault.
idiomatic: Bi told them, "Serving the throne, giving the emperor poor horses for a hunt is a small fault.

literal: Not preparing against the unexpected and letting barbarian raiders run free is a great fault.
idiomatic: Failing to guard against surprise and letting enemies raid at will is a grave fault.

literal: Now the northern Di are in full flame and the southern foes are not yet destroyed; their crafty intent watches our borders—that is my worry.
idiomatic: The northern tribes blaze with strength and the south is not yet pacified; they watch our frontiers with hungry eyes—that is what troubles me.

literal: Therefore I chose fat horses to stock the army and made distant provision against the unforeseen.
idiomatic: So I kept the strong horses for the army and looked far ahead against the unexpected.

literal: If it profits the state, why should I shun death!
idiomatic: If the realm gains by it, why should I shrink from death?

literal: An enlightened lord may be persuaded by reason; this fault is mine alone, not yours.
idiomatic: An enlightened ruler can be reached by reason; the blame is mine, not yours.

literal: Shizu heard and sighed: "To have a minister like this is the state's treasure!"
idiomatic: Shizu heard and sighed, "A minister like this is a treasure to the realm!"

literal: He was granted one suit of clothes, two horses, and ten deer.
idiomatic: He received a suit of clothes, two horses, and ten deer.

literal: Later, when the imperial carriage hunted north of the mountains and took several thousand elk and deer, an edict ordered the Masters of Writing to send five hundred cart-ox teams to transport them.
idiomatic: Later the emperor hunted north of the mountains and killed thousands of elk; he ordered the secretariat to send five hundred ox-carts to haul the game.

literal: Shizu soon told his attendants: "Pen Lord surely will not let me have them; you are not as quick as horses for hauling."
idiomatic: Shizu soon told his escort, "Pen Lord will never let this pass—you are slower than horses for hauling game."

literal: He thereupon returned.
idiomatic: He turned back at once.

literal: After traveling more than a hundred li Bi's memorial arrived, saying: "Now the autumn grain hangs yellow, hemp and beans cover the wilds, pigs and deer steal the crop, birds and geese waste it, and wind and flood also consume it—the loss mounts day and night; I beg compassionate delay so it may be gathered in."
idiomatic: A hundred li on, Bi's memorial arrived: "Autumn grain ripens in the fields, hemp and beans cover the countryside, boar and deer devour the crop, birds waste it, and wind and flood take more still—losses double by the day; grant a stay of mercy so the harvest can be brought in."

literal: Shizu told those at his side: "Pen Lord is indeed as I foresaw; he may be called a pillar of the state."
idiomatic: Shizu told his attendants, "Pen Lord is just as I predicted—a true pillar of the realm."

literal: Earlier, when Yang Nan dang came in, an edict ordered Bi to send all his sons and younger brothers to the capital.
idiomatic: When Yang Nan dang first submitted, an edict ordered Bi to send all his sons and younger brothers to the capital.

literal: Yang Xuan's younger son Wende bribed Bi with forty jin of gold; Bi took the gold, kept Wende, yet treated him without courtesy, and Wende fled to Liu Yilong.
idiomatic: Yang Xuan's son Wende gave Bi forty jin of gold; Bi accepted it, detained Wende, treated him roughly, and Wende fled to Liu Yilong.

literal: Shizu, because he was upright and had battle merit, did not add blame or punishment.
idiomatic: Shizu, weighing his uprightness and battle service, imposed no punishment.

literal: When Shizu died, the Prince of Wu was established and made Bi Minister of Works.
idiomatic: After Shizu's death the Prince of Wu took the throne and made Bi minister of works.

literal: When Gaozong ascended, he and Zhang Li both sat in council; their counsel did not accord with the imperial will and both were dismissed; there were words of resentment and slander.
idiomatic: When Gaozong came to the throne, he and Zhang Li sat in council together; their advice displeased the throne and both were removed, and resentful talk followed.

literal: Their households reported witchcraft; both suffered execution, and people of the time deemed it unjust.
idiomatic: Their families were accused of witchcraft; both were executed, and contemporaries called it a miscarriage of justice.

literal: Zhang Li was a man of Pingyuan in Yanmen.
idiomatic: Zhang Li was from Pingyuan in Yanmen commandery.

literal: [6] Skilled in accounts, Taizu knew and favored him.
idiomatic: [6] Skilled in accounts, he won Taizu's notice and favor.

literal: Taizong valued his loyal uprightness, enfeoffed him Duke of Guangping, and put him in charge of crucial affairs.
idiomatic: Taizong prized his loyal candor, made him duke of Guangping, and gave him charge of state secrets.

literal: Shizu, because of his long service and merit, employed him as a chief counselor, made him Grand Minister of Agriculture, and in great military and state deliberations Li often took part.
idiomatic: Shizu, honoring his long service, used him as a chief counselor and grand minister of agriculture; Li joined the weightiest military and civil deliberations.

literal: He was further made General Who Pacifies the North.
idiomatic: He was further made general who pacifies the north.

literal: For merit in campaigning against Helian Ding he was advanced to General Who Campaigns North.
idiomatic: For campaigning against Helian Ding he was promoted to general who campaigns north.

literal: With Prince of Le'an Fan and Duke of Jinan Cui Hui he garrisoned Chang'an, [7] frugal, fair, and of great repute.
idiomatic: With Prince of Le'an Fan and Duke of Jinan Cui Hui he held Chang'an, [7] and won high repute for frugality and fairness.

literal: On the day he left office his house had no surplus wealth.
idiomatic: When he left office his household had no surplus wealth.

literal: Shizu ordered Li to command twelve thousand troops and open the Shaquan route.
idiomatic: Shizu ordered Li to lead twelve thousand men and open the Shaquan road.

literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned in Liangzhou, the Rouran Wuti seized the moment to invade; Li with Minister of Works Daosheng repelled him.
idiomatic: While the emperor campaigned in Liangzhou, Rouran Wuti struck in his absence; Li and Minister of Works Daosheng beat him back.

literal: When Gongzong first took overall charge of affairs, Li with Duke of Dongjun Cui Hao and others assisted in government, loyal in serving the throne and speaking only on public business.
idiomatic: When Gongzong first directed government, Li with Duke of Dongjun Cui Hao and others aided the rule, loyal to the throne and speaking only on state affairs.

literal: An edict said: "Palace Attendant Duke of Guangping Li, Duke of Dongjun Hao, and others who tutor the Eastern Palace have the mature diligence of elders; We greatly commend them.
idiomatic: An edict read, "Palace attendant Duke of Guangping Li, Duke of Dongjun Hao, and others who tutor the Eastern Palace show the seasoned loyalty of elders; We commend them warmly."

literal: Each is granted one thousand bolts of cloth and silk to reward old merit."
idiomatic: "Let each receive one thousand bolts of cloth and silk in reward for long service."

literal: When Gongzong died in the Eastern Palace, Li also held the post of Grand Commandant and, bearing the staff of office, presented the posthumous edict.
idiomatic: When Gongzong died in the Eastern Palace, Li also served as grand commandant and, bearing the imperial staff, proclaimed the posthumous title.

literal: When the Prince of Wu Yu was established, Li was made Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: When Prince of Wu Yu was enthroned, Li was made grand commandant.

literal: Later, because his counsel did not accord with the imperial will, he was dismissed.
idiomatic: Later, when his counsel again missed the mark, he was dismissed.

literal: He was then executed together with Gu Bi.
idiomatic: He was executed in the same case as Gu Bi.

literal: The historiographer writes: He Ba, Xi Mu, Mo Ti, He Digan, Li Li, Liu Jie, and others all had loyal, diligent merit in campaign and still received generous appointments, yet all came to execution.
idiomatic: The historiographer writes: He Ba, Xi Mu, Mo Ti, He Digan, Li Li, Liu Jie, and the rest all fought with loyal zeal and were richly favored, yet every one was put to death.

literal: Yue, appearing in the annals amid hardship and taking office at the founding of the state, displayed both wisdom and courage and raised his fame especially high—truly the stuff of a fine general.
idiomatic: Yue, recorded in the annals through hard times and the founding crisis, showed both wit and courage and won signal fame—he was general timber of the first rank.

literal: Bi counseled armies and aided the state, with far-reaching strategy and upright feeling—he had the measure of a pillar.
idiomatic: Bi shaped armies and steadied the state, far-sighted and upright in heart—he had the bearing of a pillar.

literal: Zhang Li was sincere, cautious, and comprehensive in talent; his old merit won weight.
idiomatic: Zhang Li was sincere, careful, and rounded in talent; long service made him heavy in the court's eyes.

literal: In a hair's breadth, in one morning they perished and were overthrown; "pardons reaching ten generations" was empty talk—alas!
idiomatic: Between dawn and dusk they were ruined; "mercy for ten generations of kin" proved mere words—what a waste!

literal: Collation notes
idiomatic: Textual notes

literal: "Captured his generals Di Bozhi, Tang Xiaofang, and more than thirty others": in Beishi juan 20, Biography of He Digan, "thirty" reads "forty."
idiomatic: "Captured his generals Di Bozhi, Tang Xiaofang, and more than thirty others": Northern History juan 20, He Digan's life, reads thirty as forty.

literal: Commentary: Juan 2, Annals of Taizu, tenth month of the fifth year of Tianxing, and juan 95, Biography of Yao Chang, both read "forty"; in this biography the character "three" is erroneous.
idiomatic: Note: Taizu's annals, juan 2, Tianxing year 5 month 10, and juan 95, Yao Chang, both have forty; three here is corrupt.

literal: "The generals still did not advance": in Beishi juan 25, Biography of Liu Jie, "advance" reads "gather"; that is likely correct.
idiomatic: "The generals still did not advance": Northern History juan 25, Liu Jie's life, has advance as gather; gather is likely right.

literal: "Those who fawned on him were promoted": in various editions "advance" is corrupt as "long" and will not parse; now according to Cefu juan 338
idiomatic: "Those who fawned on him were promoted": editions corrupt advance as long, which will not parse; the text now follows Cefu juan 338

literal: 〈page 4000〉
idiomatic: folio 4000

literal: is emended.
idiomatic: and is emended accordingly.

literal: "Bi launched the armies of Shanggui, Gaoping, and Qian city to attack them": in various editions "Qian" reads "Yi"; Cefu juan 428
idiomatic: "Bi launched the armies of Shanggui, Gaoping, and Qian city to attack them": editions read Qian as Yi; Cefu juan 428

literal: 〈page 5098〉
idiomatic: folio 5098

literal: reads "Biao"; Comprehensive Mirror juan 124
idiomatic: has Biao; Comprehensive Mirror juan 124

literal: 〈page 3900〉
idiomatic: folio 3900

literal: reads "Mount Qian."
idiomatic: has Mount Qian.

literal: Hu's note: "'Mount Qian city' in the meaning ought to read 'Qian city.'"
idiomatic: Hu's note: "Mount Qian city here should be Qian city (the river-place)."

literal: In the Qin-Long region there is no "Yi city," or perhaps "Biao city."
idiomatic: In Qin-Long there is no Yi city; perhaps Biao city is meant.

literal: Qian city is the old seat of Han's Qian county, now in Long county, Shaanxi, on the key road at the Long di; juan 4, lower, Annals of Shizu, eleventh month of the sixth year of Zhenjun, records the rebel army led by Gai Wu killing the garrison commander of Qian city.
idiomatic: Qian city is the old Han seat of Qian county, now in Long county, Shaanxi, on the vital Long di pass; Shizu's annals, juan 4 lower, Zhenjun year 6 month 11, record Gai Wu's rebels killing the garrison commander of Qian city.

literal: This shows troops were stationed there.
idiomatic: That shows a garrison was posted there.

literal: At the end of Northern Wei Eastern Qin province was established at Qian city
idiomatic: Late in Northern Wei, Eastern Qin province was set up at Qian city

literal: 〈see Taiping Universal Records juan 29〉
idiomatic: (see Taiping Universal Records, juan 29)
, the annals record.

literal: "Qian" is a river name and "Qian" a mountain name, both in that region, so it is also written "Qian city."
idiomatic: The river Qian and Mount Qian both lie in that country, so the fortress is also written Qian city.

literal: "Yi" is a corruption of "Qian," and "Biao" a corruption of "Qian."
idiomatic: Yi corrupts the river-name Qian, and Biao corrupts the mountain-name Qian.

literal: Now emended to "Qian city."
idiomatic: The text is now emended to Qian city.

literal: "Bi read it": Imperial Overview juan 428
idiomatic: "Bi read it": Imperial Overview juan 428

literal: 〈page 1970〉
idiomatic: folio 1970

literal: reads "Bi read it and approved."
idiomatic: has "Bi read it and approved."

literal: Commentary: "read" and "saw" are redundant; Imperial Overview is likely correct.
idiomatic: Note: read and saw repeat; Imperial Overview is probably right.

literal: "A man of Pingyuan in Yanmen": according to juan 106, upper, Monograph on Geography, upper, Sizhou, Yanmen commandery has "Yuanping" and no "Pingyuan."
idiomatic: "From Pingyuan in Yanmen": Geography monograph juan 106 upper, Sizhou, Yanmen commandery, lists Yuanping and not Pingyuan.

literal: Yuanping was an old county of Han and Jin, recorded in successive geographies.
idiomatic: Yuanping was a Han and Jin county, recorded in every geography.

literal: Here "Pingyuan" should be "Yuanping" with the characters reversed.
idiomatic: Pingyuan here should be Yuanping with the characters reversed.

literal: "Duke of Jinan Cui Hui garrisoned Chang'an": in various editions "Hui" reads "Zheng."
idiomatic: "Duke of Jinan Cui Hui garrisoned Chang'an": editions read Hui as Zheng.

literal: Beishi juan 25, Biography of Zhang Li, and Cefu juan 406
idiomatic: Northern History juan 25, Zhang Li's life, and Cefu juan 406

idiomatic: folio 4826

idiomatic: have Hui.

literal: Commentary: Cui Hui is appended to juan 24, Biography of Cui Xuanbo; the text is now emended accordingly.
idiomatic: Note: Cui Hui is attached to juan 24, Cui Xuanbo's life; the text is emended accordingly.
